All eyes are on Anthropic, OpenAI's chief rival, and whether it will forge ahead with an IPO, perhaps as soon as this month. On Thursday, OpenAI announced what it called "a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure." Under its pledge, OpenAI said it would pay the full cost of the electricity it uses and any necessary grid improvements, do away with non-disclosure agreements with public officials (with narrow exceptions), and publish data on the jobs it expects to create. Friar said one reason she's excited for an IPO is because a market debut would be in line with OpenAI's mission to ensure artificial intelligence for all.

Anthropic's planned $1.5 trillion initial public offering is facing mounting pressure from major investors following a sharp selloff in US technology stocks, with some backers now calling for a substantially lower valuation or a possible postponement, *The Wall Street Journal* reported on Thursday. Its anticipated offering could raise as much as $100 billion, potentially making it the largest IPO in history. However, three major investors intending to participate in the offering believe the proposed valuation will have to be reduced, according to the Journal. One investor suggested the company could be valued closer to $1 trillion, representing a decline of approximately one-third from its previously anticipated price. The Nasdaq Composite suffered a severe selloff on Thursday, with companies in the index losing approximately $2.5 trillion in market capitalization as investors moved away from AI-related investments.

Nvidia did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment, and neither did China’s industry ministry or its main economic planning agency. The H200 is not Nvidia’s newest processor, but Chinese tech companies still want it to train and run large AI models. However, Beijing wants firms such as Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to use Chinese-made chips instead, according to Reuters. By the end of October, a server with eight H200 chips was being offered there for more than 6m yuan, about three times its price a year earlier. Later that month, Beijing approved a first batch of H200 imports for ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent.

They belong to Daybreak Red, the tier of OpenAI’s cyber programme for exploit development and authorised security testing. OpenAI launched Daybreak in May and said it will open GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers soon. GPT-6 Cyber is OpenAI’s fourth cybersecurity model this year, Wen Shao reported for Fortune. OpenAI said it trained the model to stay within its authorised scope, respect limits on its actions and report results accurately. In that incident, OpenAI’s AI agents broke out of a sandbox and hacked the platform. On ExploitGym, which tests whether a model can exploit a given flaw, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5%.

month.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber found 81 new Firefox flaws and is rated ‘Critical’ - The Next Web
month.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framewor...
highlights: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, up from “High” for GPT-5.6 Cyber. At first, only a select group of approved customers can use it, through the API and Codex. They belong to Daybreak Red, the tier of OpenAI’s cyber programme for exploit development and authorised security testing. OpenAI launched Daybreak in May and said it will open GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers soon. GPT-6 Cyber is OpenAI’s fourth cybersecurity model this year, Wen Shao reported for Fortune. OpenAI said it trained the model to stay within its authorised scope, respect limits on its actions and report results accurately. In that incident, OpenAI’s AI agents broke out of a sandbox and hacked the platform. On ExploitGym, which tests whether a model can exploit a given flaw, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5%.
